title: The panel read, the decline read and the case-move answer are consumed by both stories, have no contract story in the plan and no C row
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4 dependency classes and R5.5 DP table; the metadata rows of the two story lines of WP B2-S4-008 (Depends on (build) RWB-S4-E5008-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the APP; all three None for the CON; Contract, Integration and External dependencies None for both); TSD S9 v2 T-A.1 API-S9-001 GET /partners 'List partners with panel status and score' and API-S9-003/API-S9-004; TSD S4 v2 T5.2; legacy RWB-E5-008 metadata 'Depends on FEAT-PRM-02'
section: Metadata table, sections 3, 12.2, 12.8 and 13 of both stories; the C, ops_consumed and assumptions rows of both fragments
description: Both stories consume three surfaces that no metadata row carries and no plan slice owns. (1) The panel list of rwb-partner (API-S9-001), which is the only sourced operation that answers panel status and score, on the base /api/recovery/partner/v1. (2) The instruction read that answers a decline (API-S9-003 and API-S9-004 of the partner set), which is the fact of R-LIT-27. (3) The case-move answer of rwb-case, because recovery_case and the route states FIRM_SELECTION and FIRM_DECLINED are P3's and R-LIT-23 and R-LIT-27 move them. The plan gives both story lines Contract dependencies None, and no plan slice gives the two partner rows a contract story key at all, so the owner document of the panel is unnamed beyond its TSD operation row. The legacy dependency FEAT-PRM-02 is a feature row of the partner module with no story in the plan, so no C row can be derived from it either. The stories therefore build against the published documents and fakes on Day 1, keep the metadata rows exactly as the plan gives them, and record the absence here rather than inventing a story key.
evidence: WP B2-S4-008 story lines: APP H ['RWB-S4-E5008-CON', 'RWB-PLT-E1027-CON', 'RWB-PLT-N001-CON'] and C []; CON H [] and C []; both I [] and X []. TSD S9 v2 T-A.1: 'API-S9-001 | GET | /api/recovery/v1/partners | Partner portal R | E2' with purpose 'List partners with panel status and score'. TSD S4 v2 T5.2: 'Calls go through the published Java interfaces: P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents, P6 for notices'. Legacy RWB-E5-008: '| Depends on | FEAT-PRM-02 |'.
area: Contract dependencies, S4 rwb-litigation with S9 rwb-partner and P3 rwb-case
proposed: Name the rwb-partner panel and instruction reads and the rwb-case case-move answer as consumed rows of both stories, build against their published documents and fakes on Day 1 with a 2 s budget and a breaker, and let step D1 decide whether a C row and a partner contract story are added to the plan; no metadata row is changed by this WP.

title: PartnerResultSubmitted lists rwb-litigation as a consumer while DP-09 is not in this key's pattern set, so the decline cannot arrive as an event
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 43 event 21 (PartnerResultSubmitted, producer rwb-partner, consumers rwb-litigation, rwb-asset, rwb-case) and slide 19 (S4 IN: events NoticeDelivered, PartnerResultSubmitted); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 and the pattern set DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19 of both slices; legacy RWB-E5-008 AC3 and its 'Partner Portal' system column
section: Sections 2, 12.3 and 12.4 of both stories; the events_consumed key of both fragments
description: The event catalogue gives PartnerResultSubmitted three consumers including rwb-litigation, and the S4 IN row of the service card names it, so a reader may expect the decline of a firm instruction to reach this step as an event. DP-09 is not in the pattern set of either slice, neither story writes an inbox row or a subscription, and no source states that a decline of an instruction is the trigger of this event, while R-LIT-27 needs the decline as its fact. Declaring a consumer would add a pattern, an inbox and a fake that the plan does not hold; omitting the surface would leave the fact of R-LIT-27 with no path. Both stories therefore read the decline on the rwb-partner contract synchronously and declare 12.3 and 12.4 None, and the event assignment is recorded here rather than decided quietly.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 43: '| 21 | PartnerResultSubmitted | rwb-partner | rwb.partner.events.v1 | rwb-litigation, rwb-asset, rwb-case |'; slide 19 S4 IN row: 'events NoticeDelivered; PartnerResultSubmitted'. WP B2-S4-008 patterns for both slices: DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19 (no DP-09). Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-27 systems column: 'Partner Portal'.
area: Event contract, S4 rwb-litigation with S9 rwb-partner
proposed: Read the decline on the rwb-partner contract and keep 12.3 and 12.4 None in both stories; if the solution architect later adds rwb-litigation as a PartnerResultSubmitted consumer for this step, one consumed event row, one inbox subscription, one fake and one AC clause are added and no schema changes.

title: The legacy selection runs unattended while the target runs it as one step of LitigationWorkflow that no source names
source: Legacy RWB-E5-008 story statement, AC1 and AC2; FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 A2.8.2 step table and A2.8.3.3 ('None; runs unattended | Primary', 'Litigation officer | Also uses') and A2.8.4.4 ('None | No background event'); Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-LIT-08 ('Runs unattended'); Architecture v5 slides 19 and 41; Temporal and Drools Design slides 5, 7 and 20
description: The legacy story gives the feature one system step that runs unattended, the FSD describes the trigger only as 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer' and declares no background event, and the Epics 3 to 8 specification repeats 'Runs unattended'. The target runs the litigation journey in LitigationWorkflow on queue rwb-litigation, but no source names the firm-selection step, its activity, its start signal, or whether a person may start it as well. The two stories therefore read the trigger as the arrival of the pack-approved fact for a case in PACK_VERIFIED, name the step selectPanelFirm as their own design choice, and keep the officer as the actor of the screen and of the re-selection path only.
evidence: FSD S4 v3 A2.8.3.3: '| None; runs unattended | Primary |' and '| Litigation officer | Also uses |'; A2.8.4.4: '| None | No background event |'. Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-LIT-08: 'Runs unattended'. Architecture v5 slide 19: 'Temporal LitigationWorkflow (years; continues-as-new)'.
proposed: Fix the trigger as the pack-approved fact for a case in PACK_VERIFIED, evaluated in one activity selectPanelFirm of LitigationWorkflow on queue rwb-litigation under the service identity, with no officer task on the happy path and the litigation officer acting on SCR-19 and on the re-selection path.

title: The legacy story master carries no requirement identifier for RWB-E5-008
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-008 metadata table (Epic, Module, Feature, Process, Priority, Depends on, Decision and no requirement row); FSD S4 v3 Requirements served (REQ-S4-004); Business Requirements Program v4; _work/msr/plan story line of WP B2-S4-008 (reqs [])
section: Sections 2 and 18 of both stories; the reqs key of both fragments
description: The legacy story of RWB-E5-008 names its feature FEAT-LIT-08 and its prerequisite FEAT-PRM-02 and no requirement identifier, and the plan carries an empty requirement list for both slices. The requirement the feature serves is REQ-S4-004, 'A law firm is selected from the panel by rule using panel performance, and instructed through the partner portal', of the FSD S4 requirements-served list and of the Program BRD, and it covers both the selection and the instruction. Both stories therefore trace to REQ-S4-004, to FEAT-LIT-08 and to the L3 process 08 Litigate and enforce, and the story states that the identifier comes from the FSD and not from the legacy master.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E5-008 metadata table: '| Epic | E5, release 31 March 2027 | | Module | S4 Litigation and enforcement | | Feature | FEAT-LIT-08 ... |' with no requirement row. FSD S4 v3 Requirements served: '| REQ-S4-004 | A law firm is selected from the panel by rule using panel performance, and instructed through the partner portal. | Must | E5 |'.
proposed: Trace both stories to REQ-S4-004, record that the legacy master carries no requirement ID, and let the traceability manager add the reverse link when the RTM is next versioned.

title: The rule rows of R-LIT-23 and R-LIT-27, their scorecard weights, capacity test, court set, conflict check and accept window, and the D7 level have no content in any source read for this key
source: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-LIT-23 and R-LIT-27; TSD S4 v2 T4 (the table stops at R-LIT-25 with 'and 54 more'); FSD S4 v3 A2.8.3.1 (VR-S4-008-1, R-LIT-23, R-LIT-27, BR-S4-008 only); Architecture v5 slides 14, 27 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R3 default ruling (rule package registry to P7)
description: R-LIT-23 and R-LIT-27 are two of the 79 LITIGATION rules over 38 states, and the TSD S4 T4 table stops at R-LIT-25 with 'and 54 more', so their rows, their version and their test cases live only in the rules workbook and in the registry. The rules name the facts they test - the scorecard, capacity, court coverage, conflict, the 2-working-day window and the D7 decision level - and no source gives any of them a weight, a threshold, a court set, a conflict rule or a content. The registry, the rule rows and the package version are rwb-decision's under the R3 default ruling, and the four-eyes approval of a package is there as well. Both stories therefore name the two rows and declare none of their values, load the package on RulePackageInForce and record the version they used.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4: '| R-LIT-23 | Litigation | D7 | PACK_VERIFIED | PACK_APPROVED | pack_verified_at set | Select the law firm by rule from the panel | FIRM_SELECTION | Workbench | Rules component, partner performance data | Same day |' and '| R-LIT-27 | Litigation | D7 | FIRM_INSTRUCTED | INSTRUCTION_DECLINED | the firm declines, or does not accept inside the window | Record the decline and re-select the next firm on the scorecard | FIRM_DECLINED | Workbench | Partner Portal | 2 working days |'; TSD S4 v2 T4: '| and 54 more | | | | |'.
area: Rules, S4 rwb-litigation with P7 rwb-decision
proposed: Have rwb-decision publish the two rule rows, the package version, the scoring and capacity parameters, the court coverage set, the conflict rule and the accept window as versioned reference data and rule rows; until then both stories load the package on RulePackageInForce and carry the values as data, never as constants.

title: The score, capacity, court coverage and conflict fields of a panel firm have no field list and no operation name, and the legacy v_ace_score read has no grant in this service
source: Legacy RWB-E5-008 Data table (partner DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007, partner_instruction DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016, v_ace_score DF-ACE-270 to DF-ACE-279); TSD S9 v2 T3.1 and T-A.1; TSD S4 v2 T3.1 and T-A.1; FSD S4 v3 A2.8.3.1; Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-05
description: R-LIT-23 tests the scorecard, the capacity, the court coverage and the conflict status of a panel firm, and the sources give the panel firm seven fields and the instruction nine, none of which carries a score, a capacity figure, a court set or a conflict status. The panel list of the partner service declares 'panel status and score' in its purpose and no field list, and no source names the operation of the panel read in a target contract. The legacy data table also lists v_ace_score (DF-ACE-270 to DF-ACE-279), and rwb-litigation holds no v_ace_* grant, so DP-05 applies as a prohibition and the score facts can only arrive on the owner's contract. Both stories therefore carry the four facts as elements of the rwb-partner answer, add no column to legal_action, and mark the field list and the operation names with the placeholder.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E5-008 Data table: '| partner | id, partner_code, partner_name, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end and 1 more | DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 |' and '| v_ace_score | score_key, account_key, model_code, model_version, score_value, estimate_value and 4 more | DF-ACE-270 to DF-ACE-279 |'; TSD S9 v2 T3.1 partner fields DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 (no score, capacity, court or conflict column); TSD S9 v2 T-A.1 API-S9-001 purpose 'List partners with panel status and score'; TSD S4 v2 T3.1 legal_action DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014.
area: Data and contract, S4 rwb-litigation with S9 rwb-partner and P1 rwb-source-data
proposed: Carry the score, capacity, court coverage and conflict status as facts of the rwb-partner panel answer only, add no column to legal_action, hold no v_ace_* grant, and fix the field list and the two operation names with the rwb-partner owner before the baseline is tagged.

title: VR-S4-008-1 tests the freshness of the ACE batch of the source, and rwb-litigation holds no ACE view to test it
source: FSD S4 v3 A2.8.3.1 (VR-S4-008-1 and MSG-P1-001); Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-05
section: Sections 8, 14 and 19 of the APP story; sections 13, 14 and 19 of the CON story
description: The FSD validation rule VR-S4-008-1 tests the freshness of the data product after a late or failed ACE batch for its source, reading the legacy v_ace_batch_status, and raises MSG-P1-001. rwb-litigation holds no v_ace_* grant, and the ACE view contract, the extension tables and the freshness stamp are rwb-source-data's. The rule therefore cannot be evaluated in this service, and no source states which service raises the message for this step or on which contract a freshness answer reaches it. Both stories carry MSG-P1-001 in their message set and show it where the owner reports staleness, and neither adds a freshness read.
evidence: FSD S4 v3 A2.8.3.1: '| VR-S4-008-1 | Data product stale after a late or failed ACE batch for its source (v_ace_batch_status) | MSG-P1-001 {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |'; Architecture v5 slide 29 (no v_ace_* grant for rwb-litigation) and slide 41 (the ACE view contract is P1's).
area: Data, S4 rwb-litigation with P1 rwb-source-data
proposed: Apply VR-S4-008-1 where the ACE data product is read, in rwb-source-data and rwb-partner, carry MSG-P1-001 in the message set of both stories and show it on SCR-19 where the owner reports staleness; add a freshness read to section 12.2 only if the solution architect decides this service must test it itself.
